Question: Which node in the generative model represents the latent variable?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 1, page 4) (image attached): Figure 1: Figure 1a presents the generative story of our model. Figure 1b illustrates the inference net- work using the reparametrization trick to perform variational inference on our model. Shaded nodes are observed; double circles indicate deterministic transformations of parent nodes.
Words printed in the figure: w y η θ r α c B Ni D (a) Generative model r µ σ π c y w ϵ linear linear D (b) Inference model
[E2] (figure, Figure 1, page 4): a zoomed view of Figure 1 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: Figure 1a presents the generative story of our model where shaded nodes are observed and others are unshaded.

cites.quote: Figure 1a presents the generative story of our model.

claims.text: In the generative model diagram (Figure 1a), the unshaded nodes representing latent variables include alpha, r, B, and the double-circled deterministic transformations theta and eta.

cites.observation: In the generative model subfigure (a), the unshaded nodes are alpha at the top, r below it, B to the right, and double-circled nodes theta and eta.
